summary: Extended the healed-partition case so the applied-state path the account left unexercised is measured, and registered the successor execution. After the two sides are reconnected, one client entry is driven into whichever instance leads, then the case reports the first index at which the two sides' stores disagree, both sides' applied positions, each instance's FSM contents for the two divergent payloads and the new payload, and a derived divergent_applied_same_index field, with two new sources (a node applies its own log's entries up to the commit index; a new leader dispatches its no-op entry) and two new materials anchored in raft.go. Verified locally (go vet clean; focused run of TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed): with the flag enabled the stores still disagreed at log index 118 (first side LogConfiguration, second side LogCommand), both sides had applied through 121, and the post-heal entry committed at 121 and was applied by the restarted instance and both peers, so two state machines held different applied values for one log index while the cluster kept serving clients; with the flag disabled no index disagreed and both sides applied to 119. Submission validated (valid true, execution requested): six comparisons - the two healed predicates and their control, the applied-divergence predicate with its flag-disabled control, and a continuation predicate requiring the post-heal entry to reach every instance's FSM.
